sections.h2: Who bills property tax on a Bloomington house
sections.html:
The bill comes from McLean County, not the city. Bloomington is the county seat, and one office, the treasurer and tax collector, mails a single bill for each of about 68,000 parcels, collecting for nearly 200 taxing districts. Find it at the Government Center, 115 E. Washington Street, Room M101, or call (309) 888-5180.

Valuing the property is handled elsewhere. Inside the city, the City of Bloomington Township assessor sets values. Equalization and exemptions belong to the Supervisor of Assessments, the chief county assessment officer, at (309) 888-5130, and complaints go to the Board of Review. City hall sends no property tax bill, although it registers rental buildings and collects its own local taxes.

  • Treasurer: payments, duplicate bills, delinquent tax and the yearly tax sale.
  • Assessors: values, property record cards, exemptions and mailing address updates.
  • Board of Review: assessment complaints, at (309) 888-5132.

An estimated 78,804 people lived here in 2025, a 0.1% rise from 78,680 in 2020. Homeowners occupy 61.9% of occupied homes and the rest, roughly 38 in 100, are rentals, a fact worth knowing if an investor may buy your house. The typical owned home is valued at $203,300, with median rent of $1,050 a month.

Normal is Bloomington's neighbor. Bloomington District 87 and McLean County Unit District 5 teach most students in the city, with small portions in Olympia District 16. The district name on your bill shows which applies to you.

Installments fall due in the first week of June and the first week of September, with all dates subject to change. Under 35 ILCS 200/20-15, a bill that never showed up does not erase the tax. No bill by mid-May? Ask the treasurer for a duplicate.

Typical McLean County collection calendar
TimingEvent
Early MayReal estate bills mailed
First week of JuneFirst installment due
First week of SeptemberSecond installment due
Early OctoberLast day to pay in the office by personal check
Following business day$10.00 certified fee and delinquency letters
Early NovemberJudgment hearing; last day to pay to avoid the sale
Day after judgmentDelinquent tax sale begins at 10:00 a.m.

Interest on a late payment is 1.5% a month, beginning the day after the due date. Postmark by the due date and you are on time.

The office will not take partial payments, and it sends no receipt unless you request one. Your canceled check or bank statement is proof enough.

  • By mail to the lockbox: McLean County Collector, P.O. Box 843637, Kansas City, MO 64184-3637.
  • In person, Monday to Friday from 8:00 to 4:30, at the Washington Street address above.
  • Drop boxes stay open day and night, by the Washington Street side of the lot or the East Street entrance.
  • Online or by phone with a credit card (a convenience fee applies), or by annual automatic withdrawal.
  • At a participating local bank.

Once the October personal check cutoff passes, only certified funds work, and the office takes nothing on sale day. State law charges a mortgage company $5.00 for a duplicate bill. After a refinance or payoff, send the Supervisor of Assessments a change of address so bills find you.

The Board of Review accepts a complaint for 30 days after the township's notice runs in the newspaper, and that notice gives your township's equalization factor. Bloomington Township is a different township in the same county with its own notice and factor, so find out which one holds your parcel before relying on a deadline or a number.

Assessments draw on the three years of market value before January 1 of the assessment year, then an equalization factor moves the result to 33.33%. Nothing late gets heard. Nonfarm owners file form PTAX-230, and the Board sits inside the Government Center in the Supervisor of Assessments' office.

A state disaster declaration after severe storms lets owners of damaged homes apply for reassessment on form PTAX-245. If yours took damage, ask the assessor whether that process is open now.

An exemption trims taxable value ahead of the rate, so what you save follows your tax rate. Only your primary residence counts.

  • General homestead: up to $6,000, first filed with the county assessment office.
  • Homestead improvement: up to $75,000 of market value, or $25,000 assessed, usually granted automatically for four years.
  • Senior citizens: $5,000, with an initial PTAX-324 and proof of age.
  • Low-income senior freeze: household income under $75,000, using PTAX-340, which the county mails each year around February 1 to current senior exemption holders.
  • Disabled persons: $2,000, renewed each year by December 31.
  • Returning service members: $5,000 for the year of return and the following year.
  • Disabled service members: $2,500, $5,000 or up to $250,000, depending on the rating.

Seniors can ask the treasurer about deferral at (309) 888-5180. Buyers file their own claims once the sale closes.

Rental owners inside the city limits register every year through the city's Rental Property Program. Cost is $65 a building, with $5 more per unit once a building has three or more, and each registration lasts through December 31.

New owners cannot inherit a registration, so a buyer files again. Renting or occupying a covered building also requires a Certificate of Inspection. If a building is rated "fair," the city may ask for a $5,000 letter of credit or pledged account until it passes. Follow-up inspections run $100 per appointment and a missed one costs $75. Clear open violations before listing, because they feed a buyer's repair requests.

Illinois bills tax after the fact, so a house sold during the year still has bills to come. The seller usually gives the buyer a credit at closing for the share built up, and the buyer pays the next bill. Get the title company to show in writing how the credit was figured, and verify the parcel's payment status before you sign. If a prior installment was missed, the unpaid bill stays attached to the parcel, which is why the check matters.

Before you list, pull your latest bill, your exemption confirmations and any rental registration paperwork into one folder. A buyer and the title company will ask for each of them.

If you pay through a mortgage escrow, confirm shortly before each due date that the lender has paid. After a payoff, update your mailing address with the Supervisor of Assessments so notices reach you.

faqs.q: Which office do I call about a Bloomington property tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the McLean County treasurer at (309) 888-5180 for payments and duplicate bills, and the county assessor at (309) 888-5130 for values, exemptions and mailing addresses. The city of Bloomington does not send the bill.

faqs.q: When is the second installment of Bloomington property tax due?
faqs.a: In the first week of September each year. Interest of 1.5% per month starts the day after the due date.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Bloomington assessment?
faqs.a: You get 30 days from the newspaper notice for your township, and a late complaint is not heard. Look for the notice every year.

faqs.q: Does Bloomington require rental registration when I sell?
faqs.a: Registration belongs to the owner, and the city says it cannot transfer to a new owner. A buyer of a rental registers anew and pays the printed fee of $65 per building.

faqs.q: Can I pay McLean County tax with a card?
faqs.a: Yes, online or by phone, with a convenience fee. The office also accepts mail, in-person payments, a 24-hour drop box, local banks and annual automatic withdrawal.
